stem: At the same temperature and pressure, what volume of $\text{O}_2$ is required to completely react with $5.6$ L of $\text{CO}$?

verdicts.working: Balanced equation: 2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂. At the same temperature and pressure, gas volumes follow the mole ratio, so O₂ needed = 5.6 × 1/2 = 2.8 L.

working:
$2\text{CO} + \text{O}_2 \longrightarrow 2\text{CO}_2$
At equal temperature and pressure, gas-volume ratio $\text{CO} : \text{O}_2 = 2:1$.
$V(\text{O}_2) = 5.6 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 2.8$ L

Independent check: Balanced equation: 2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂. At the same temperature and pressure, gas volumes follow the mole ratio, so O₂ needed = 5.6 × 1/2 = 2.8 L.
solution:
$$2\text{CO} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2$$
At the same temperature and pressure, gas volumes are in the ratio of their coefficients: $\text{CO} : \text{O}_2 = 2:1$.
$$V(\text{O}_2)=5.6\times\frac{1}{2}=2.8\text{ L}$$
